questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It was a place to improve my spanish. 
I found the history of Chile and current political tensions interesting. 
There is a department of geography, that offers courses, which I find interesting and fit with the rest of my bachelor program.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find information about entering the country with visa, covid-stuff ect. Especially with the helo of the international student office at Universidad de Chile (PME).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received a lot of assistance from the PME team. Where the assistance was lacking, was at my faculty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Orientation from my faculty was very lacking, especially since there is a lot of difference between faculties, which made it hard for the PME team to guide us on specific issues. We didn't have any official orientation at my faculty (FAU).

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing through friends of friends, so I'm not quite sure, how much I can advice on this. Maybe reaching own in ones own network and see if someone knows someone, who knows someone, ect - who rents a room. But I know I have quite some friends here who found housing in other ways.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Santiago has a lot of different districts, and if one has the chance, take your time to explore a bit some of them (being aware of recommendations for safety), before signing a contract for the rest of the semester. I wish I had done so.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was no housing available to students as far as I know.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Registrering to the institution itself was easy. But the proces of registrering for courses was quite long in the end.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Registrering to the institution was something we did online with guidance from the university. Quite easy. 
Registrering to courses was done through an email to the PME team. What made it a bit complicated was that course descriptions from many faculties came out late, and they had to move deadlines. Then some 1 or 2 weeks after we could delete courses. This was also done via email through PME. 
What made everything a bit confusing was that our registration on the universities online platform (like absalon in copenhagen university) - u-cursos - was very slow, which meant the first week(s), we had very little information (international students), though students and teachers at the faculty were very helpfull.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The PME team were very helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get the classes I wanted most.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't get stressed about it - everything will happen with time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one course with a very high (nice) level.  2 with which the level could have been higher, mainly due to teachers repeating themselves a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
What I missed the most was exercises, which we have quite a lot of at UCPH, but they were completly absent in my courses at Universidad de Chile. 
The teaching style is more like class-room-teaching and reminds me a bit of gymnasium.
I felt quite some professors spend way too much time talking about "nothing" and well essentially because of this starting the classes very late. Though it could just be an overrepresentation among the professors I had. I noticed there is a stronger hierarchy between students and professors, than I'm used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Electivo de especialización: Lugar, territorio, identidad colectiva y movimientos sociales
Análisis y evaluación ambiental
Gestión integral de cuencas

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Well I really liked my elective about social movements. Then I also enjoyed my course on watersheet management. I would probably recommend getting into the electives it seems professors and students are more motivated there.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: That I used more money arriving the first month, since I was going out more to get to know people and not knowing the cheapest way to do things. Also since Chile is not that cheap and especially travelling can easily get expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was way more expensive than expected. And travelling.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There wasn't really much or anything as far as I know. More so political meetings and events arranged by students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Like officially arranged from our university for all students I don't remember much. I remember a talk about gender - which was very interesting. And a talk about the proposed new constitution, but this I believe was arranged by students. 
I believe some people are arranged in some football. 
Then there were a lot of social activities arranged by students for exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Since I don't remember anything that was more established, I'm not quite sure. I would recommend to go to one of these social activities for exchange students to get to know some people who are also on exchange.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Cajon de Maipo. It is super close to Santiago and there are really good climbing opportunities. 
Also with a good bus connection from Santiago is Valparaíso, which is super charming. 
For longer holidays I can recommend from own experience: Chiloé, La Selva Valdiviana and San Pedro de Atacama (or more so the area around).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go with what comes up. And of course being open and friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Could be cheak-kissing, but honestly I got used to that pretty quickly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That it has so many different things and consists of so many different cultures.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- When choosing courses you can choose more than you need and eliminate later. Use this to see the teaching style of the professors, and then not only choose according to subject, but also professor, since there are quite some differences. 
- Coming from UCPH things usually work quite "according to the book" and everything is on time. This is not my experience at my faculty, FAU, at UdC. But that's okay. Just taking all of this more relaxed, people at the university are generally quite flexible. 
- Get to know your fellow students at university. This has been for me the easiest way to get to know chileans, and I believe it can be more interesting than staying in the environment of exchange students, even if that is also quite a lot of fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Santiago is a huuuge city. There is plenty to explore.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friendships, cultural exchange and better spanish.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To begin with I thought it was hard to get to know people. But I believe it also teaches, that these things just take some time. And well people are easier to talk to, when the weather gets warmer.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
